name: Tarvostrigaranus

attributes.attribute: an obscure god from the Continental Celtic world
shown as a bull with three cranes upon him
known from two stone sculptures, at Paris and at Trier
may be the same as or similar to the god Esus

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tarvostrigaranus is an obscure Continental Celtic god. He is also called Tarvos Trigaranus. Two stone sculptures show him. One is at Paris. The other is at Trier. He appears as a bull with three cranes on his back. The birds may be other waterbirds. He may be like the god Esus, or the same god as Esus.

okr.objective: Describe the Continental Celtic god Tarvostrigaranus.
key_results: Two stone sculptures, at Paris and Trier, show him as a bull with three cranes.
He is also called Tarvos Trigaranus.
